training-data.name: Training Data
training-data.bio: Podcast: LIVE: Jensen Huang on Building the Dynamo of the Intelligence Age

html_en:
The AI industry's center of gravity is shifting from models to systems — from what AI knows to what AI does, and who owns the institutional loops that make it compound over time.

🏭 Jensen's Sermon: From Data Centers to Intelligence Factories

If you want the clearest articulation of why NVIDIA sits at the center of this moment, Watch/Listen: Jensen Huang on Building the Dynamo of the Intelligence Age. In a sprawling live conversation, Huang walked through computing history with the patience of a very good professor — and the confidence of someone whose chips are in everything.

"Two years ago, AI was able to understand you and generate information — that was interesting, novel, a little cute. Whenever you need a poem written, great way to do it. Who doesn't want to write a country song? But now because it's able to do work, AI is valuable. We pay for people who do work." — Jensen Huang

The framing is simple but sharp: we don't pay know-it-alls, we pay workers. AI has crossed that threshold. Huang's downstream implication — that traditional "data centers" are really just retrieval systems, and that the new AI factory is something categorically different, generating intelligence on demand rather than fetching stored files — reframes the entire infrastructure investment thesis.

"Every time I say something to it, I give it new information — context, a query. Between the context and the query, it will understand, reason about it, and produce an output based on that circumstance." — Jensen Huang

🔁 The Learning Loop: The New Corporate Moat

The most resonant idea circulating today isn't about a specific model or product — it's about compounding. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's framing, flagged by @swyx and amplified hard by @amasad (2,900+ likes) and Aaron Levie, is becoming the enterprise AI mantra of the week:

"The real opportunity is not in picking the best model but instead in building a learning loop on top of models where human capital and token capital compound. You can offload a task, or even a job, but you can never offload your learning. The future of the firm is the ability to compound that learning across people and AI." — Satya Nadella, via @swyx

Levie's gloss on this is worth reading in full — he sees the applied AI layer, not the model layer, as where durable value accumulates:

"A company should be able to switch out a 'generalist' model without losing the 'company veteran' expertise built into their learning system... so much of the power and value will accrue to wherever can best leverage any AI system against their information." — @levie

Garry Tan adds the sovereignty angle: "Open source is the escape hatch for businesses to be able to continue to control their own destiny long term." Which dovetails neatly with Levie's separate observation that the DeepSeek moment — where a model was briefly pulled back — has given every non-US government a fresh incentive to go open-weights.

🤖 Agentic Everything: Subagents, Goals, and Yakshaves

On the practitioner side, @swyx is one of the few people publicly stress-testing Anthropic's Claude Code (formerly "Ultracode") in the wild, and his early read is characteristically precise:

"This thing is scarily good at burning tokens but you need to set up your repo to parallelize properly to make use of the fanout that subagents are best at. Basically the idea is 'subroutines but intelligent.' When you understand just how much knowledge work is just yakshaves after yakshaves that require some judgment and intelligence, you start to appreciate that dynamic workflows are not just for coding tasks." — @swyx

Meanwhile, @thsottiaux dropped a quietly fascinating observation about OpenAI's Codex that lit up the timeline (2,200+ likes): the agent can now see and set its own /goal.

"Everything we build, we build also as a tool for the agent. This is a generalization of meta prompting, where you let the agent set its own task based on your intent." — @thsottiaux

Self-directed goal-setting in deployed agents is one of those details that sounds incremental and is actually a fairly significant architectural crossing. The agent isn't just executing — it's interpreting intent and instantiating its own objectives. Garry Tan sees this as the generational divide to watch: "The next generation of young people who change the world will almost certainly be the people who are most adept at making long-running multi-stage multi-team agent tasks work extremely well."

🛠️ Skills, Not Prompts: A New Folk Wisdom Emerges

One of the more useful pieces of craft knowledge making the rounds today comes from @zarazhangrui, on building AI "skills" (reusable, bottled workflows):

"You don't make a good skill by writing a skill. You make it by doing the thing, fixing it 20 times, then telling the AI to bottle up everything you just did." — @zarazhangrui

It's a small insight with big implications: the best human-AI collaboration artifacts aren't designed top-down, they're distilled from iteration. This aligns with @rauchg's note that his platform has now passed 700,000 community-created skills — "all organic and community-driven." The open ecosystem is quietly becoming a massive corpus of codified human judgment.

And @thenanyu offers the shortest possible reframe of the pair programming debate: "Counterpoint: everyone pair programs now, with a robot." Hard to argue.
html_zh:
从AI工厂到学习飞轮，今天的核心主题只有一个：AI的价值，正从"能理解"升级为"能干活"——而真正的竞争，将在谁能把自己的知识积累进系统里见分晓。

🏭 Jensen Huang：AI工厂，历史上最大的基础设施建设

如果你想理解当下AI浪潮的物理底座，没有比 Jensen Huang 这场演讲 更清晰的入口了。Watch/Listen: LIVE: Jensen Huang on Building the Dynamo of the Intelligence Age

黄仁勋用一条极简的历史弧线解释了为什么现在是转折点：两年前的ChatGPT只是"生成"——输入文字，输出文字，新奇但不值钱。而今天的AI，能够推理并完成工作。这个区别，是他整个论述的核心。

"两年前，AI能理解你、生成信息，这很有趣、很新颖，有点可爱。你想写首诗？很好用。但现在，因为它能干活，AI才真正有价值……我们今天按小时付钱给AI。这是人类历史上增长最快的软件生意。"
— Jensen Huang

他进一步把计算机的历史一刀劈开：过去六十四年，计算机本质上是一个检索系统——存数据、取数据，所以那些建筑叫"数据中心"而不是"计算中心"。而AI工厂代表的是一种全新的计算范式：每次交互都在实时生成，而不是调取存档。这个底层逻辑的转变，正是他认为当前基础设施投资规模如此巨大的根本原因。

🔄 Satya与Levie：真正的护城河是"学习飞轮"

如果说Jensen讲的是基础设施层，那么今天另一条高热度的讨论线，来自微软CEO Satya Nadella的一篇文章——被 @swyx、@amasad（"这是我见过的最鼓舞人心的AI企业正和愿景"）和 Box CEO Aaron Levie 相继转发，引发广泛共鸣。

"这是人类第一次能在人与数字系统之间建立真正的认知循环。这改变了我们对企业内部工作的整体认知方式……真正的机会不在于选出最好的模型，而在于在模型之上构建一个学习飞轮，让人力资本与算力资本共同复利增长。你可以外包一项任务，甚至一份工作，但你永远无法外包你的学习。"
— Satya Nadella，via @swyx

Levie 对此深表认同，并补充了一个关键架构洞察：

"一家公司应该能够随时换掉'通用'模型，而不会失去已经构建在学习系统里的'公司老兵'专业知识。"
— @levie

这个框架其实给了企业一个清晰的战略方向：与其焦虑于哪家模型最强，不如专注于把自己的知识、数据和流程"编码"进可迭代的智能系统。Applied AI层，而非模型层，将成为价值积累的主战场。

🤖 Agentic时代的实操：子智能体与"技能"的正确打开方式

理论层面讲完飞轮，实操层面的讨论同样热闹。@swyx 分享了对 Anthropic Claude 的 ultracode（多智能体并行编程工具）的第一手观察：

"这东西烧token的速度很吓人，但你需要正确设置你的代码仓库才能充分利用子智能体最擅长的'扇出'能力。基本思路是'子程序，但有智能'。当你意识到多少知识工作不过是一层套一层的琐碎任务（yak shave），而每一层都需要一点判断力时，你就会明白动态工作流不只适用于编程任务……"
— @swyx

与此同时，@thsottiaux 分享了一个关于 OpenAI Codex 的有趣细节：Codex 现在可以自己设定自己的目标（/goal），这是元提示词（meta prompting）的一次泛化——让智能体基于你的意图，自主生成自己的任务。这条推文获得了超过2200个点赞，是今日技术讨论中传播最广的一条。

在"技能"（skill）的构建方法论上，@zarazhangrui 给出了一个反直觉但实用的建议：

"你不是通过'写一个技能'来做出好技能的。你是通过先把事情做出来，修了20次之后，再让AI把你刚才做的一切'装瓶'——这才是做出好技能的方式。"
— @zarazhangrui

🔓 开源：地缘政治压力下的战略逃生舱

今天还有一条值得关注的讨论暗线，由 @levie 和 @garrytan 共同点燃。起因是近期一个此前纯属理论的风险变成了现实：一个模型可以被随时从某个国家的用户面前撤走。

"开源是企业长期掌控自身命运的逃生舱。"
— @garrytan

Levie 则进一步从国家战略层面展开：如果任何时候一个模型都可能对某国用户不可用，那些国家就有充分理由去发展主权AI——而目前开源权重模型的主要来源，并非美国。他认为，美国在思考AI监管时，应该在"模型层"与"应用层"之间做出清晰区分，避免在错误的层面施力，反而削弱了自己在全球AI生态中的领导地位。

这场讨论没有结论，但它提出了一个越来越重要的问题：在AI基础设施高度集中的时代，"技术主权"究竟意味着什么？
